recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中除了一般小血小板外，可見一顆與紅血球差不多大、充滿紫色顆粒且無細胞核的巨大血小板，箭頭指向貼在紅血球上的小紫色顆粒狀物，用來練習區分血小板與紅血球內含物或巨大顆粒。
features: Giant platelet approaching red cell size with abundant purple granules and no nucleus (left panel)
Small normal platelets scattered, some overlying or abutting red cells (arrows)
Inset: small dense purple granular body adjacent to a red cell
Adjacent mononuclear cell (lymphocyte) with pale cytoplasm for size comparison
Red cells largely normocytic with central pallor
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, two fields with an inset. Red cells are largely normocytic and normochromic. A giant platelet approaching the size of a red cell, with abundant azurophilic granules and no nucleus, is present next to a lymphocyte. Arrows mark small granular purple bodies lying on or beside red cells, which on close inspection have the appearance of platelets rather than true intraerythrocytic inclusions. The image alone does not establish the specific underlying disorder referenced by the title; findings should be interpreted with platelet count and clinical history.

ddx.vs: A Howell-Jolly body is a smooth, round, uniformly dense nuclear remnant within the red cell plane, whereas a platelet is granular with a pale halo and often lies over the cell edge.
Parasites show a blue cytoplasmic ring with a red chromatin dot inside the red cell, not a solid granular purple body.
Separation requires platelet count, Dohle-like neutrophil inclusions (MYH9) and flow cytometry for GPIb, not morphology of a single giant platelet.
